Creates a job (POST /jobs). With --wait N the request is held up to N seconds (≤ 60) for
the result: a succeeded job's data is printed as JSON on stdout and a summary on stderr.

Exit codes: 0 succeeded (or still running), 2 failed or canceled, 3 parked, waiting for an
input or for attention.

Usage:
  kaab jobs run (--url URL --extract @schema.json | --program NAME[@VERSION] [--input k=v]...) [flags]

Examples:
  kaab jobs run --url https://example.com --extract '{"title":"h1"}' --wait 30
  kaab jobs run --program acme-report@production --input report_id=42 --session acme --wait 60

Flags:
      --dry-run                  stop before the first side-effect step
      --extract string           the extract schema: @file.json, - (stdin) or inline JSON
  -h, --help                     help for run
      --idempotency-key string   the Idempotency-Key (a ULID by default)
      --input stringArray        a program input, name=value (repeatable; JSON values are parsed)
      --max-tier string          the highest tier the job may use: http, browser or apex
      --program string           a program reference: name, name@3, name@production, prg_…, pv_…
      --session string           a stored session to run in
      --tag stringArray          a tag (repeatable)
      --url string               the page of a shorthand job
      --wait int                 seconds to wait for the result (1–60)
      --webhook-url string       where the job's events are delivered

Global Flags:
      --base-url string   API base URL (KAAB_BASE_URL; https://api.kaab.ist/v1 by default)
      --json              print the API's JSON instead of a table
      --profile string    profile to use (KAAB_PROFILE; the current profile by default)
      --test              use the profile's test-mode key (sk_test_)
